items.answer: Deliver the WL mapping for Indicator 2 (days with delay) and Indicator 3 (delays in 12 months) as pure functions plus exported option lists. Success = each dropdown option maps to the WL in the POC acceptance criteria, tests pass with node --test.
items.source: JOB request, Requirements table REQ-03-02 / REQ-03-03
items.quote: Build only these two requirements

items.answer: No end users or roles in this slice: it is a library of pure functions consumed later by POC screens built by other parts; no role-based access.
items.quote: No UI in this slice.

items.answer: In: REQ-03-02 and REQ-03-03 (option lists + WL functions in src/indicators). Out: Indicator 1 and its collapsing of indicators 2-3, any UI, counting of delays (caller does it).
items.quote: Indicator 1 (repayment delay yes/no) and its collapsing of indicators 2–3 are OUT of scope here.

items.answer: Yes: the table gives WL per option (>3 days=2, >60=3, >90=4; 1=1, >1=2) and C2 gives the zeros; all values concrete, so each option has a testable expected WL.
items.quote: "no delay" and "<=3 days" → WL 0; Indicator 3 "0" → WL 0.

items.answer: Only wording differences: the POC table writes '≤3 days' while C1 fixes the string '<=3 days'; C1 (confirmed by business) wins. The overlapping labels (>3, >60, >90) are not a conflict: the caller picks one option, each maps to exactly one WL.
items.quote: Dropdown values are exactly these strings

items.answer: No priority order: the two requirements are independent and ship together in this slice (two parallel developers).
items.quote: They are independent of each other.

items.answer: daysWithDelay.mjs: export const DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS (5 strings in order: 'no delay','<=3 days','>3 days','>60 days','>90 days'), export function daysWithDelayWl(option) -> 0|2|3|4. delayCount.mjs: export const DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS ('0','1','>1'), export function delayCountWl(option) -> 0|1|2. Input is a string, trimmed with String.prototype.trim(), exact case-sensitive match; empty/other/non-string -> RangeError.
items.quote: `export const DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS` (the 5 strings, in order) and `export function daysWithDelayWl(option)` → 0 | 2 | 3 | 4

items.answer: Any value not in the list after trim (including empty string, wrong case, inner-whitespace change, null/undefined/number) throws RangeError. Success returns the WL integer; no fallbacks.
items.quote: a non-string input is a RangeError too

items.question: Is the RangeError message text part of the contract?
options: Not specified; tests assert only the error type (RangeError)
Fixed message format, e.g. include the offending value
items.impact: Only the type is stated; if the message must be fixed tests and devs need the exact text. Recommended: type only.

items.question: Should the exported *_OPTIONS arrays be frozen (immutable) so screens cannot mutate them?
options: Object.freeze the arrays (safer, still an array of strings in order)
items.impact: Internal robustness only; no change to values, order or WL mapping. Recommended: freeze.
